title: Burst slab allocator and overage smoothing ledger for Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated customers occasionally need short-lived throughput increases for traffic spikes. Current mechanisms either allocate large reserved capacity (slow, expensive) or allow uncontrolled overrun with opaque invoice spikes. Goal: provide a bounded, observable short-burst mechanism that (1) guarantees micro-throughput increases for minutes-to-hours without long-term reservation, (2) attributes cost predictably and smooths invoice signals, and (3) exposes operator controls for per-fleet and per-tenant constraints.

Proposal: implement a 'burst slab' allocator + smoothing ledger. A burst slab is an ephemeral quota slab that can be attached to a Dedicated fleet for a configured window (e.g., 5m, 1h). Each slab has: capacity (tokens/sec), duration, amortization policy, and usage meter. The smoothing ledger converts raw slab consumption into an amortized billing charge that can be spread across billing periods and optionally capped by customer-configured grace amounts.

Design highlights:
- Slab lifecycle: request -> provisional allocation -> activation -> consumption -> settle. Requests can be triggered by autoscaler signals, operator UI, or tenant-initiated API.
- Autoscaling integration: autoscaler will prefer scaling nodes when predicted tail-latency breach > threshold; if cold-starts would exceed SLO, the autoscaler can request a short slab as fallback.
- Operator controls: console UI to pre-authorize slab pools per tenant, set per-tenant max slab concurrency, define default amortization windows (e.g., 24h, 7d), and opt-in invoice smoothing.
- Billing smoothing math: compute raw token-cost for slab usage, then spread (linear amortization) over the chosen window with metadata tags for audit. Provide immediate invoice preview and a separate 'burst ledger' line-item for transparency.
- Safety: soft-guard that will preempt slab traffic if cold network/infra failures risk noisy neighbor effects; fallbacks to reduced-rate model variants.

Non-goals: not a replacement for long-term reserved capacity. Not targeting per-token spot pricing optimizations in this ticket.

API changes: POST /v1/dedicated/fleets/:id/burst-slabs {capacity, duration_minutes, amortization_days, owner, reason}. Response includes slab_id, provisional boolean, estimate_cost.

Metrics to emit: slab_request_count, slab_activation_latency_ms, slab_consumed_tokens, slab_amortized_cost_cents, slab_preempt_events, slab_fallback_rate. Dashboards linked below.

Rollout plan: feature-flag behind 'burst_slab' for 10% of Dedicated fleets -> progressive ramp to 50% after 2 weeks of monitoring -> GA. Billing smoothing off by default for pilot tenants; require opt-in.

Migration: existing ad-hoc surge handlers will be adapted to request slabs rather than enabling global burst pools. Provide a migration script and operator checklist.

Runbook excerpt: if slab_activation_latency spikes > 2s for 5m, disable provisional allocations and route requests to fallback model; notify SRE on-call and open incident with tag 'burst-slab'.

acceptance_criteria: API to create provisional slab returns 200 with estimate and slab_id
Autoscaler can request slab and observe activation within configured SLA (<= 3s median)
Console shows per-fleet active slabs and allows operator revoke/pre-authorize
Billing ledger emits amortized line-items and invoice preview matches sample spreadsheet within 1%
End-to-end e2e test that simulates spike and verifies graceful fallback when slab preempted
comments: 2025-02-12 - Asha Patel: Initial design doc posted to Confluence; flagged billing team for input on amortization options.

2025-02-18 - Priya Khanna: Billing reviewed amortization model — prefers 7-day default amortization to reduce invoice noise for trials. Suggested adding explicit 'customer_accepts_overage' flag for legal audit.

2025-02-24 - Luca Moreno: Implemented provisional API prototype (see PR #1427). Activation latency median at 1.8s in ci-load but 4.1s in stage under heavy metascheduling; investigating kernel selection path.
2025-02-27 - Data: Load test 2025-02-26 attached — observed slab_preempt_events when two concurrent slabs targeted same AZ; added per-AZ slab fencing to design.
2025-03-03 - Ops: Suggested default max concurrent slabs per-tenant = 2 and default cap = 2x baseline throughput to limit cost exposure.
implementation_notes: Server-side: new SlabManager service that persists slab state in time-series + Postgres; keep slab usage in Redis counters for fast reads.
Autoscaler change: add SlabAdvisor plugin that recommends slab sizes based on recent p95 token/sec and cold-start forecasts.
Billing: create BurstLedger processor job that converts time-windowed usage into amortized invoice events; tie to cost-center tags.
Console: extend Fleet detail page with 'Burst Slabs' tab and operator actions (revoke, pre-authorize, billing preview).
Testing: synthetic spike harness in staging using kafka-traffic-replayer to validate activation and fallback.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy neighbor if slabs concentrate on single AZ -> Mitigation: per-AZ slab fencing and spread allocation algorithm.
Risk: billing disputes from rapid amortization swings -> Mitigation: invoice preview, opt-in smoothing pilot, and detailed burst ledger export.
Risk: slab activation bottleneck -> Mitigation: cache pre-provisioned micro-slabs and warm quick-path in runtime kernels.
Risk: operator confusion -> Mitigation: add clear UI explanations and a one-click revert for slab changes.
